note:
Talks about eradication of screw worm.

Screwworm females mate once, so the strategy is to breed male screwworms, sterilize them, then drop them in a region so that females mate with the sterilized male and lay eggs that don't hatch.

The screwworm population is relatively low, with a range of 35m on average (but can be longer, up to 180m?).

To breed and sterilize, hamburger, water and formaldehyde are mixed at the right temperature to breed pupae. The pupae are then irradiated enough to sterilize but not kill. Batches are created and then released.

By the mid 1960s, screwworm had been eradicated from the US and a barrier had been pushed below Mexico.

It looks like a confluence of conditions in late 2010s led to screwworm breaking through the established barrier. Covid made inspection of cattle lax and operation of screwworm facilities more inconsistent. The rain forest that was wild has started to be cultivated in addition to cartels and other illegal activity transporting cattle across the barrier.
